_comment: Measurement-shaped figures that carry no ISO date in their own paragraph.
The preferred fix is always to date the figure inline — '_measured 2026-08-10_' beside the
number, where a reader sees it. This registry is for the cases where an inline date would be
wrong: a figure quoted as an illustration rather than as evidence, or one whose date belongs to
'kind' and 'reason' are required. kind=measurement additionally requires an ISO 'measured'
date, because that is what makes it evidence. kind=illustration does not, because demanding a
date for an anecdote only produces a fabricated one -- which is the failure this check exists
to catch, moved somewhere less visible.

entries.reason: An anecdote motivating the rule that a current count belongs nowhere -- 'on one stack a memorised multiplier moved by more than 100x inside a quarter'. It is not offered as evidence and has no single measurement date; the source is an un-versioned host config file, so no date can be recovered honestly.
Quoted as the example of a stale docs claim ('a README claiming 28 tests against a suite of 29'). Dating it would suggest the figure is being asserted rather than criticised.
Two occurrences: a qualitative rate ('~100% false-positive') and a reliability column in a mechanism-comparison table. Neither is a count taken on a day.
Arithmetic on two constants in the same sentence -- 182 animals x 141 adjectives. Derived, not measured; it changes only when the word lists change.
